# Autoloads

The services the foundation runs as autoloads. A game has the core's and those of the modules its `game.json` lists; `node tools/link.js` writes them into its `project.godot` in this order: the core's first group, the modules' (a module after the modules it requires), the core's second group, then the game's own. A module's autoloads come from `gamebase/gamebase.json`.

| Autoload | Layer | Script | What it does |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Transition` | core | `gamebase/core/world/scene_transition.gd` | Changes the scene behind a fade: the screen covers while the scene loads (on a thread where the platform has them; a web build without threads loads it when the change is asked for), the scene changes, and the screen clears again. `WorldTravel` changes locations through it. |
| `GameSettings` | core | `gamebase/core/settings/game_settings.gd` | The player's settings: the volumes, the display, autosave, how fast text types out, hints, accessibility, the language and the bindings of the controls (`bindings`). It applies them to the audio buses, the window, the translation server and the input map, and writes them to `settings_path` (JSON) once the frame of a change is done: a slider dragged across writes once a frame, not once a step. The file is replaced whole (`JsonFile`), so a crash never leaves half of it. |
| `InputPrompts` | core | `gamebase/core/input/input_prompt_service.gd` | Which device the player is using, keyboard and mouse or a gamepad, and the text that names the key, button or stick of a control on it ("E", "A", "Left Stick") for the HUD and the interaction prompts. The bindings come from `GameSettings.bindings`; this service reads them and never changes them. |
| `InputLock` | core | `gamebase/core/input/input_lock.gd` | Who holds the player's controls and the world's pause, by reason. A menu, a dialogue, a minigame or a cutscene takes a lock under a reason of its own and gives it back when it is done. The player acts only while no reason holds a lock, and the world (the scene tree) is paused while any lock that pauses is held. Locks add up, so one that ends never frees what another holds: a menu that closes while a minigame runs leaves the world paused. |
| `GameEvents` | core | `gamebase/core/events/game_events.gd` | The core's notifications: the short status line (toast) the game's HUD shows, and the hints the player reads once (`HintData`). What happens in a module's systems is announced on that module's own `<Module>Events` autoload (`LifesimEvents.crop_harvested`). |
| `GameRules` | core | `gamebase/core/rules/game_rules.gd` | Registry of the conditions and actions content can name in text. |
| `GameStats` | core | `gamebase/core/stats/game_stats.gd` | Numbers the game's systems read and other systems change: the energy a tool costs, how long a fish takes to bite, how hard an attack hits. |
| `GameRandom` | core | `gamebase/core/random/game_random.gd` | The world's randomness: one seed per game, and from it a separate stream for each thing that rolls dice, named by a key (`"weather:12"`, `"fish:3:0:river"`). |
| `WorldClock` | core | `gamebase/core/time/game_clock.gd` | The world's date and time: the day, counted from 1, and the minute of that day. It runs on real time while the world is not paused, and other systems follow it through `day_changed`, `hour_changed` and `minute_changed` (crops, shipping, mail, NPC schedules). How the days group into seasons and weeks, how fast minutes pass and when night falls is the game's `GameCalendar`. |
| `WeatherState` | core | `gamebase/core/time/weather_system.gd` | The weather of each day (`WeatherData`), rolled from the world's seed (`GameRandom`) and the chances the game gives per season (`GameDefinition.weather_odds`): the same world has the same weather on the same day, however often it is asked or loaded. A day the odds give no other weather has the game's `GameDefinition.clear_weather_id`; a game that names none has no weather (an empty id, and no `WeatherData`). |
| `ContentDB` | core | `gamebase/core/content/content_registry.gd` | Indexes the running game's content by kind and id, and checks it. |
| `GameModules` | core | `gamebase/core/modules/game_modules.gd` | Installs every `GameModule` the game links, then has `ContentDB` index and check the game's content and `GameRules` check the conditions and actions it names, now that every module registered its kinds and rule keys. A release build only indexes: its content passed the checks before it shipped. |
| `Vitals` | core | `gamebase/core/player/player_vitals.gd` | The player's vitals (`VitalData`), each between 0 and its maximum: work and attacks spend them (`spend()`, `try_spend()`), food and rest restore them, enemies drain them. The HUD follows `changed`; `depleted` fires when one reaches 0, and what follows (a defeat at no health) belongs to the module that owns the vital. |
| `WorldState` | core | `gamebase/core/world/world_state.gd` | The world's memory for one game: named values (flags, counters and the state of things in the world) that content and services keep under a key, such as a rule's `SET_FLAG` or a farm plot's crop. Many module services keep all their state here rather than in a save section of their own. |
| `GameProfile` | core | `gamebase/core/profile/game_profile.gd` | The player's profile: what they achieved and unlocked across every save of the game. Starting a new game, loading a save or deleting a slot leaves it as it is. It holds the unlocked achievements (`AchievementData`) and profile flags, booleans and counters as `WorldState` holds a world's, and writes them to `profile_path` before the next frame after a change. |
| `CombatEvents` | combat | `gamebase/modules/combat/combat_events.gd` | What happened in the combat module, for higher modules and the game to react to (quests, collections, skill experience, sounds). Only the combat module emits these. An argument named `<kind>_id` (or ending in `_<kind>_id`) is the id of an entry of that kind of content (`GameEvent`). |
| `PlayerDefeat` | combat | `gamebase/modules/combat/defeat/player_defeat_service.gd` | Defeats the player when their health (`CombatSettings.health_vital_id`) runs out: they pass out (`GameSession.pass_out()`, cause `GameSession.CAUSE_DEFEAT`), lose `CombatSettings.defeat_money_loss_percent` of their money and wake at home the next morning with every vital full. The defeat is announced as `CombatEvents.player_defeated`. Health that runs out while the player already passes out for another cause, or that a save holds at 0, defeats them once that is over or once play starts. |
| `DialogueManager` | dialogue | `addons/dialogue_manager/dialogue_manager.gd` | From the addon of that name. |
| `Dialogue` | dialogue | `gamebase/modules/dialogue/dialogue_service.gd` | Shows one conversation at a time in a `DialogueBalloon` in the current scene: the lines of a dialogue file from one of its titles (`show_dialogue()`, read by the `DialogueManager` addon) or those of a chat made while it runs (`show_chat()`). Any system shows one this way: an NPC's talk (`ConversationService`), a sign or a camp's keeper (`DialogueSpot`). |
| `ItemsEvents` | items | `gamebase/modules/items/items_events.gd` | What happened in the items module, for higher modules and the game to react to (quests, collections, skill experience, sounds). Only the items module emits these. An argument named `<kind>_id` (or ending in `_<kind>_id`) is the id of an entry of that kind of content (`GameEvent`). |
| `InventoryState` | items | `gamebase/modules/items/items/inventory_store.gd` | A slot-limited inventory. |
| `Wallet` | items | `gamebase/modules/items/wallet/wallet_service.gd` | The player's money: shops, shipping and rewards move it, and it never drops below 0 (`spend()` refuses, and returns false, when there is not enough). The HUD follows `money_changed`. It is saved with the game, and a new game starts with the game's `ItemsSettings.start_money`; a save slot shows it. |
| `Hotbar` | items | `gamebase/modules/items/hotbar/hotbar_service.gd` | The player's quick-select slots: which item id sits in each slot and which slot is selected. Slots hold item ids, not items; the inventory owns the items. |
| `BuffState` | items | `gamebase/modules/items/buffs/buff_service.gd` | The food buffs (`FoodBuffData`) the player has active and the world minute each one ends. While a buff runs, its multipliers and bonuses change the game's stats: this service is a `GameStats` source. |
| `ShopState` | items | `gamebase/modules/items/shop/shop_service.gd` | Buying from shops and selling to them: it checks the price (`ShopData`), the player's money (`Wallet`) and the room in the inventory (`InventoryState`), moves the money and the items together, and tells the player the result with a toast. |
| `CraftingState` | items | `gamebase/modules/items/crafting/crafting_service.gd` | Crafting items from recipes (`RecipeData`): a recipe can be crafted when its condition holds and the player carries its ingredients, and crafting it swaps the ingredients for the result in the inventory (`InventoryState`) in one step. |
| `StorageState` | items | `gamebase/modules/items/storage/storage_service.gd` | What each storage container (a chest, named by its container id) holds, and the moves between it and the player's inventory (`InventoryState`). A container holds stacks of each item's stack size, in as many slots as the caller allows (24 by default). |
| `BuildingState` | items | `gamebase/modules/items/building/building_placement_service.gd` | The structures the player places in the world (`PlaceableData`, such as a chest, a furnace or a sprinkler): which stand where in each location, and whether a new one may go at a spot. Each time the scene changes it builds the current location's structures under a `PlacedStructures` node. |
| `LifesimEvents` | lifesim | `gamebase/modules/lifesim/lifesim_events.gd` | What happened in the lifesim module, for higher modules and the game to react to (quests, collections, skill experience, sounds). Only the lifesim module emits these. An argument named `<kind>_id` (or ending in `_<kind>_id`) is the id of an entry of that kind of content (`GameEvent`). |
| `EventState` | lifesim | `gamebase/modules/lifesim/calendar/calendar_event_manager.gd` | Which calendar events (`CalendarEventData`, such as a fair or a market) are on at the world clock's day and minute, and the yearly reward for taking part in one. It checks every event again each minute and announces each start and end (`event_started`, `event_ended`). |
| `ShippingState` | lifesim | `gamebase/modules/lifesim/economy/shipping_service.gd` | The shipping bin: items the player ships leave the inventory at once and are paid for overnight, at their `sell_price`, when the world clock's day changes. It holds what waits in the bin and the last day it paid out. |
| `FarmExpansionState` | lifesim | `gamebase/modules/lifesim/expansions/farm_expansion_service.gd` | The farm expansions (`FarmExpansionData`, such as a big coop or barn) the player has bought, and whether the next one can be bought. A bought expansion raises how many animals its housing holds, which `AnimalState` reads through `get_capacity()`. |
| `MineState` | lifesim | `gamebase/modules/lifesim/mining/mine_run_state.gd` | The mine: the floor the player is on and the deepest floor they reached, from 1 to `MAX_FLOOR`, kept by a `DepthTrack` (`mine:depth`, `mine:deepest` in `WorldState`), so they are saved with the world and a new game starts on floor 1. The first floor counts as reached from the start. It also lays out each generated floor's rocks and enemies from the game's `floor_table` (`MineFloorTable`), and gives the elevator its stops: floor 1 and every `CHECKPOINT_STEP`th floor down to the deepest. |
| `AnimalState` | lifesim | `gamebase/modules/lifesim/animals/animal_ownership_service.gd` | The farm animals the player owns (`FarmAnimalData`): which housing each lives in and in which slot, its name, and its daily state (when it was last fed, petted or gave a product). It buys, sells, renames and feeds them, and knows how many more each housing holds. |
| `FishingState` | lifesim | `gamebase/modules/lifesim/fishing/fishing_service.gd` | A fishing cast from start to catch: the player casts at a location, waits for a bite and reels in during the bite window, by pressing interact or by winning the game's reel minigame (`reel_minigame_id`). The fish that bites is rolled from the fish (`FishData`) available at that location, day, time and weather. |
| `LateNight` | lifesim | `gamebase/modules/lifesim/rest/late_night_service.gd` | Sends a player who stays up too late home: at the game's late night minute (`LifesimSettings.late_night_minute`), a player still in the world passes out (`GameSession.pass_out()`) and wakes at home the next morning with what a night's sleep refills full, but only part of their energy (`LifesimSettings.late_night_energy_percent`). A wait (`GameClock.advance_until()`) ends at that minute too, while a player is up. |
| `CollectionState` | lifesim | `gamebase/modules/lifesim/collections/collection_service.gd` | The player's collection log: how many of each item they have harvested, caught, mined, collected from animals, processed, foraged and shipped, one category each (`CATEGORIES`), and how many items each category holds in the game's content. It counts them by itself from the modules' events (`LifesimEvents`, `ItemsEvents`, `ShippingState`). |
| `CollectionMilestones` | lifesim | `gamebase/modules/lifesim/collections/collection_milestone_service.gd` | The collection milestones (`CollectionMilestoneData`): rewards for discovering a number of a category's items in `CollectionState`, or for claiming a set of other milestones. It tells the player when one is ready and pays its reward (items and money) when they claim it. |
| `DailyContractState` | lifesim | `gamebase/modules/lifesim/contracts/daily_contract_service.gd` | The town's daily contract on the notice board: one request at a time to forage, catch, mine, harvest or ship a number of one item, for money. An offer is picked with the world's seed for its day (`GameRandom`) among the items the player can still get before it is due: in season, in the coming weather, on a mine floor they have reached. |
| `NpcAi` | npc_ai | `gamebase/modules/npc_ai/ai/npc_ai_service.gd` | The lines NPCs chat with (`NpcAiChat`). It builds each request from what the NPC knows (`NpcContext`) and remembers (`NpcMemory`: the latest messages and the older ones that bear on what the player says, `NpcMemoryRecall`), and answers requests one at a time in the order they come: from the game's language model (`NpcAiSettings.endpoint`) once the player allows online services, else, or when the model answers nothing or takes longer than the settings allow, from the rules the game wrote (`NpcRuleProvider`). Every request gets an answer, so a chat works offline and never waits for long. It saves nothing. |
| `NpcSocialEvents` | npc_social | `gamebase/modules/npc_social/npc_social_events.gd` | What happened in the npc_social module, for higher modules and the game to react to (quests, collections, skill experience, sounds). Only the npc_social module emits these. An argument named `<kind>_id` (or ending in `_<kind>_id`) is the id of an entry of that kind of content (`GameEvent`). |
| `RelationshipState` | npc_social | `gamebase/modules/npc_social/npc/relationship_manager.gd` | The player's friendship with each NPC, in points (`POINTS_PER_HEART` make a heart, up to `MAX_HEARTS`), and the daily limits on raising it: the first talk of the day with an NPC gives 10 points, and each NPC takes one gift a day. |
| `HeartEvents` | npc_social | `gamebase/modules/npc_social/npc/heart_event_service.gd` | Which heart events (`HeartEventData`, an NPC's scripted scene at a number of hearts) the player has seen, and which one is due when they talk to an NPC: the unseen event that matches the NPC's hearts, the location, the day and the time, lowest hearts first. |
| `NpcMemory` | npc_social | `gamebase/modules/npc_social/npc/npc_memory_store.gd` | What each NPC remembers of the player: the latest messages of their conversations (up to `max_recent_messages` per NPC, each with its day, time and place) and named facts, such as the last day they talked or a heart event seen. `NpcContext` puts this memory in what an NPC knows when it talks. |
| `NpcContext` | npc_social | `gamebase/modules/npc_social/npc/npc_context_service.gd` | What an NPC knows when it talks: who it is, the relationship, the world, the player and its memory, then what every module the game has tells about its own systems (`GameModule.get_facts()`: the player's inventory, the events under way, the quests), each section under its own key. A section named as one of the context's own keys (npc, relationship, world, player, ...) is left out. |
| `ConversationService` | npc_social | `gamebase/modules/npc_social/npc/conversation_service.gd` | Starts a conversation with an NPC: it notes the talk in the NPC's memory (`NpcMemory`), builds what the NPC knows (`NpcContext`) and shows the dialogue (`Dialogue`): a due heart event (`HeartEvents`) first, else, for an NPC that chats (`NpcProfileData.ai_enabled`) in a game with a module that makes chats (`chat_maker`: npc_ai), its chat, else the NPC's lines for its hearts. A heart event counts as seen once its dialogue was read to the end. The service saves nothing of its own. |
| `ProgressionEvents` | progression | `gamebase/modules/progression/progression_events.gd` | What happened in the progression module, for higher modules and the game to react to (quests, collections, skill experience, sounds). Only the progression module emits these. An argument named `<kind>_id` (or ending in `_<kind>_id`) is the id of an entry of that kind of content (`GameEvent`). |
| `QuestState` | progression | `gamebase/modules/progression/quests/quest_manager.gd` | The player's quests (`QuestData`): which have started, how far each objective has come and which are done. An objective moves on by itself as its event fires (`QuestObjective`): a crop harvested, a talk with an NPC, a mine floor reached, whatever module announces it. It listens only to the events of the active quests' objectives, and not while a save is restored or a new game resets the services (`GameSession.is_changing()`), which is not play. A quest pays its reward (items and money) once every objective is met. |
| `MailState` | progression | `gamebase/modules/progression/mail/mail_service.gd` | The player's mailbox: it delivers each letter (`MailData`) once its condition holds, and keeps which letters arrived, which were read and whose reward (items and money) was claimed. |
| `UpgradeState` | progression | `gamebase/modules/progression/upgrades/tool_upgrade_service.gd` | Upgrading a tool into a better one (`ToolUpgradeData`): when the upgrade's condition holds and the player has the tool, the materials and the money, it takes them and gives the new tool, all together or not at all, and puts the new tool in the old one's `Hotbar` slots. |
| `TownProjects` | progression | `gamebase/modules/progression/projects/town_project_service.gd` | The town's community projects (`TownProjectData`): the player donates the items a project asks for from the inventory, and once every item is in, the project is complete and its reward (items and money) can be claimed. A project opens once the projects it requires are complete. |
| `RunState` | roguelite | `gamebase/modules/roguelite/runs/run_service.gd` | Runs: a stretch of play that starts, say at a dungeon's entrance, and ends with an outcome, the player back at camp (`OUTCOME_RETURNED`), defeated (`OUTCOME_DEFEATED`) or taken out of play by passing out for another cause (lifesim's late night), a load, a new game or the title (`OUTCOME_ABANDONED`; passing out then saves what the run brought, the others do not). It counts the runs a world started and keeps values that last one run (`set_value()`), cleared when a run starts and when it ends, and gives each run its own random streams (`stream()`). |
| `RtsEvents` | rts | `gamebase/modules/rts/rts_events.gd` | What happened in the rts module, for higher modules and the game to react to (quests, collections, sounds). Only the rts module emits these. An argument named `<kind>_id` (or ending in `_<kind>_id`) is the id of an entry of that kind of content (`GameEvent`). |
| `Skills` | skills | `gamebase/modules/skills/skill_manager.gd` | The player's experience and level in each of the game's skills (`SkillData`), and the stat changes of the perks those levels unlock: a source of `GameStats`. |
| `TacticsEvents` | tactics | `gamebase/modules/tactics/tactics_events.gd` | What happened in the tactics module, for higher modules and the game to react to (quests, collections, sounds). Only the tactics module emits these. An argument named `<kind>_id` (or ending in `_<kind>_id`) is the id of an entry of that kind of content (`GameEvent`). |
| `WorldTravel` | core | `gamebase/core/world/world_travel.gd` | Moves the player from one location (`WorldLocationData`) to another: it changes to the location's scene behind the `Transition` fade and puts the player on the named spawn point (`WorldSpawnPoint`), or the location's default one, with the view on them at once (`place_player()`). |
| `GameAudio` | core | `gamebase/core/audio/game_audio_service.gd` | Plays the game's music and sounds by cue (`AudioCueData`): one music track at a time on the Music bus and up to `SFX_CHANNEL_COUNT` sounds at once on the Sounds bus. Each location plays its own music (`WorldLocationData`) when the scene changes, and each event listed in `GameDefinition.event_cues` plays its cue. |
| `SaveManager` | core | `gamebase/core/save/game_save_manager.gd` | Writes and restores the game in save slots. |
| `AutoSave` | core | `gamebase/core/save/auto_save_service.gd` | Saves the game on its own: every `interval_seconds`, after each travel, when the player passes out (`GameSession.pass_out()`) and when the window closes, while `GameSettings.autosave` is on and the game can be saved. It writes the active slot's autosave, which leaves the player's own save as it was (`SaveManager.write_save(true)`). A save that works shows on the game's `SaveIndicator`; one that fails tells the player why with a toast. |
| `GameSession` | core | `gamebase/core/session/game_session.gd` | The game from the title screen to play and back: it starts a new game (each service's new-game step in order, then the start location), continues the selected slot's save through `SaveManager`, and returns to the title. It also counts the time played, and takes the player out of play to wake at home when a module knocks them out (`pass_out()`: combat's defeat, lifesim's late night). While the session changes (`is_changing()`: a new game is set up or a save loads), what the services announce is not play; `play_started` marks the end of it. |
| `Playthrough` | core | `gamebase/core/playthrough/playthrough_service.gd` | The playthrough: the first, or a later one that carries part of the one before it over (new game plus). What carries over is the game's `GameDefinition.inheritance`, each an `InheritanceRule` (a share of the money, the items with a tag, the skills' experience): when the player starts the next playthrough (`start_next()`) each rule takes its part of the game as it is, and the new game the session then starts gives it back once its services are reset. The playthrough's number saves with the game, and content asks for it with `PLAYTHROUGH_AT_LEAST`. |
| `MiniGameHost` | core | `gamebase/core/minigames/minigame_host.gd` | Runs one minigame at a time above the world: |
| `GameTriggers` | core | `gamebase/core/rules/game_triggers.gd` | Runs the game's triggers (`TriggerData`): listens to every event a trigger names and, when one fires, runs the actions of each trigger on it whose condition holds. The condition and the actions see the event's arguments by name under the context's "event" key. What the services announce while a save is restored or a new game resets them is not play and fires nothing. |
| `GameDiagnostics` | core | `gamebase/core/diagnostics/game_diagnostics.gd` | Prints one line of diagnostics to the game's output and log (`GAMEBASE_DIAGNOSTIC` and JSON) at startup and when a save, a load, an autosave or a travel fails: the game and engine versions, the system, the language, the save slot, the day and time, and the location. `SupportBundle` puts the same context in its summary. |
| `SupportBundle` | core | `gamebase/core/diagnostics/support_bundle_service.gd` | Makes a support bundle the player can send with a bug report: a zip file, in `user://support` unless a path is given, with a summary (versions, settings and bindings, and an outline of each save slot) and the end of the newest game logs. |
